mcqs.question: Consider the linear equation 2x + 3y = 6. Which of the following descriptions correctly represents its graph on the xy‑plane?

options.A: A straight line passing through points (0,2) and (3,0).
options.B: A straight line passing through points (0,-2) and (3,0).
options.C: A straight line passing through points (0,2) and (-3,0).

mcqs.answer: A straight line passing through points (0,2) and (3,0).
mcqs.explanation: Setting x = 0 gives 3y = 6 ⇒ y = 2, so the y‑intercept is (0,2). Setting y = 0 gives 2x = 6 ⇒ x = 3, so the x‑intercept is (3,0). The line joining these intercepts is the graph of 2x + 3y = 6. Options B, C give wrong intercepts and D is not a straight line.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand solution of a pair as common point
mcqs.question: Two linear equations  x - 2y = 4  and  3x + y = 7 are plotted on the same set of axes. What does the point where the two lines intersect represent?

options.A: The sum of the solutions of the two equations.
options.B: The ordered pair (x, y) that satisfies both equations simultaneously.
options.C: The point where the slopes of the two lines are equal.
options.D: The average of the x‑intercepts of the two lines.

mcqs.answer: The ordered pair (x, y) that satisfies both equations simultaneously.
mcqs.explanation: The intersection point satisfies both equations at the same time; therefore it is the common solution of the pair. Options A, C and D describe unrelated quantities.

mcqs.question: A student claims that if two straight lines intersect, the system of equations they represent must have infinitely many solutions. Which option correctly addresses this misconception?

options.A: The statement is true because intersecting lines share all points.
options.B: The statement is false; intersecting lines meet at exactly one point, giving a unique solution.
options.C: The statement is true only when the lines are perpendicular.
options.D: The statement is false; intersecting lines always represent inconsistent systems.

mcqs.answer: The statement is false; intersecting lines meet at exactly one point, giving a unique solution.
mcqs.explanation: Two distinct non‑parallel lines intersect at one point only, which corresponds to a single ordered pair that satisfies both equations. Hence the system has a unique solution, not infinitely many. Options A, C and D are incorrect statements.

mcqs.question: Which condition guarantees that the graphs of the equations 4x - 5y = 10 and 8x - 10y = k are parallel lines?

options.A: k = 20, making the two equations represent the same line.
options.B: k ≠ 20, ensuring the lines have the same slope but different intercepts.
options.C: k = 0, which makes the second line pass through the origin.
options.D: k = 5, which makes the second line perpendicular to the first.

mcqs.answer: k ≠ 20, ensuring the lines have the same slope but different intercepts.
mcqs.explanation: Multiplying the first equation by 2 gives 8x - 10y = 20. The left‑hand sides of both equations are proportional, so they have the same slope. For the lines to be parallel (not coincident) the constants must not be in the same ratio; therefore k must not equal 20. Option B states this condition. Options A gives coincident lines, C and D are unrelated.

mcqs.question: Given the equations (i) 3x - 6y = 9 and (ii) x - 2y = 3, which of the following statements is correct regarding their graphs?

options.A: The two lines are intersecting and meet at a single point.
options.B: The two lines are parallel but distinct.
options.C: The two lines are coincident, representing the same line.

mcqs.answer: The two lines are coincident, representing the same line.
mcqs.explanation: Multiplying equation (ii) by 3 yields 3x - 6y = 9, which is identical to equation (i). Hence both equations describe the same straight line; they are coincident. Options A, B and D describe different relationships.

mcqs.learning_point: Relate graph position to number of solutions
mcqs.question: In the graphical method of solving a pair of linear equations, which of the following graph positions corresponds to the system having infinitely many solutions?

options.A: The two lines intersect at exactly one point.
options.B: The two lines are parallel and never meet.
options.C: The two lines coincide, lying on top of each other.
options.D: One of the lines is vertical and the other is horizontal.

mcqs.answer: The two lines coincide, lying on top of each other.
mcqs.explanation: When the two lines are coincident, every point on the line satisfies both equations, giving infinitely many ordered pairs as solutions. Option A gives a unique solution, B gives no solution, and D still yields a single intersection point.

mcqs.question: What does it mean to represent a linear equation graphically?

options.A: Drawing a curve that shows all possible solutions of the equation.
options.B: Plotting a straight line whose points satisfy the equation.
options.C: Creating a table of values without drawing any line.
options.D: Sketching a parabola that passes through the origin.

mcqs.answer: Plotting a straight line whose points satisfy the equation.
mcqs.explanation: A linear equation in two variables describes a straight line on the xy‑plane; each point on that line satisfies the equation. Options A and D describe non‑linear graphs, while C does not involve a graphical representation.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand solution of a pair as common point
mcqs.question: When two linear equations are solved together, what does the common point of their graphs signify?

options.A: The point where the two equations have different solutions.
options.B: The ordered pair that satisfies only one of the equations.
options.C: The ordered pair that satisfies both equations simultaneously.
options.D: The point where the slopes of the two lines are equal.

mcqs.answer: The ordered pair that satisfies both equations simultaneously.
mcqs.explanation: The intersection (common) point of the two lines is the pair (x, y) that makes both equations true at the same time; it is the solution of the system. Options A and B are incorrect statements, and D describes a condition for parallelism, not intersection.
